nodes.name: Theorem 1.2.1: Main
nodes.statement:
Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
    \item 
   $\mathrm{Ram}(E/F) \subseteq \mathrm{Spl}(K/F)$, $\mathrm{Ram}(K/F) \subseteq \mathrm{Spl}(E/F)$.
    \item 
    For $v \in \mathrm{Inert}(E/F) \cap \mathrm{Inert}(K/F)$, $\mu_v$, $\psi_{v}$ are unramified 
    and $j \in \mathcal O_{E,v}^\times$.
    \item Any archimedean and $2$-adic place of $F$ is split in $L$.
    \item 
   $\mathrm{Ram}_F(\Pi) \cap \mathrm{Inert}(E/F) \cap \mathrm{Inert}(K/F) = \emptyset$.
    \item There exist $v_1 \in \mathrm{Spl}(E/F), v_2 \in \mathrm{Spl}(L/F)$ such that $\Pi$ is supercuspidal at all places above $v_1$ and $v_2$.
\end{enumerate}
Then the following are equivalent as predicted by [TwistedGGP]:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item The Asai $L$-value $L(\frac 12,\Pi,\operatorname{As}_{L/E} \times \mu^{-1}) \ne 0$.
    
    \item There exists a skew-Hermitian space $V$ of
    dimension $n$ over $E$, and a cuspidal automorphic 
    representation $\pi$ of $\mathrm{U}(V)(\mathbb A_K)$ such that $\operatorname{BC}(\pi) = \Pi$, and the period
    integral  $\mathcal P(f,\phi) = \int_{[\mathrm{U}(V)]}
         f(h)\overline{\Theta(h,\phi)}\, dh\ne 0$
for some $f \in \pi$, $\phi \in \mathcal S(\mathbb L(\mathbb A))$.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Proposition 4.2.3: Fundamental
nodes.statement:
Suppose $[\gamma, x, y] \in X_{\textnormal{rss}}$
    matches with $[\zeta, z] \in Y_{\textnormal{rss}}^{V^+}$,
    and that $\gamma$ and $\zeta$ are Kottwitz.
    Then
    \[
        \mathrm{Orb}([\gamma, x, y], \widetilde f', \phi') =
        \omega([\gamma, x, y])
        \mathrm{Orb}([\zeta, z], f, \phi_1 \otimes \phi_2).
    \]
    If $[\gamma, x, y]$ matches with
    $[\zeta, z] \in Y_{\textnormal{rss}}^{V^-}$, with
    $\gamma$ and $\zeta$ Kottwitz, then
    \[
        \mathrm{Orb}([\gamma, x, y], \widetilde f', \phi') = 0.
    \]

nodes.name: Proposition 5.1.1: Global representatives
nodes.statement:
Let $k \ge 0$ be an integer.
Suppose $\gamma_0 \in \textnormal{S}_{n,L/K}$ is
regular semisimple and normal, and let $\delta
= \gamma_0\sigma_{L/E}(\gamma_0)^{-1}$. 
Then there exists $\gamma \in \textnormal{S}_{n,L/K}$ with
$\gamma\sigma_{L/E}(\gamma)^{-1} = \delta$,
such that $\gamma$ is Kottwitz at all places $v$ of $F$ 
which are inert in $E$ and unramified in $K$, and
$k$-Kottwitz at $v_1, v_2, \dots, v_m$.

nodes.name: Theorem 5.3.3: RTF identity
nodes.statement:
Let $\Pi$ be the base change of $\pi$.
For good matching test functions $(f',\phi')$
and $\{(f^V,\phi_1^V \otimes \phi_2^V) \}_{V\in [\mathrm{SHerm}_n^\times(F)]}$, we have
    \[
        I_\Pi(f', \phi') =
        \sum_{V \in [\mathrm{SHerm}_n^\times(F)]} \sum_{\pi'} J_{\pi'}^V(f^V, \phi_1^V \otimes \phi_2^V),
    \]
where $\pi'$ runs over all irreducible cuspidal
automorphic representations of $\mathrm{U}(V)(\mathbb A_K)$
whose base change to $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb A_L)$ is also
$\Pi$.

nodes.name: Theorem 6.1.2: Asai $L$ -functions
nodes.statement:
There exists $\varphi \in \Pi$ and
$\phi' \in \mathcal S(\mathbb A_{E,n})$ such that
$\lambda(\frac12, \varphi, \mu, \phi') \neq 0$
if and only if $L(\frac12, \Pi, \mathrm{As}_{L/E}\times
\mu^{-1}) \neq 0$.

nodes.name: Proposition 5.2.4: Unitary spectral decomposition
nodes.statement:
If the test function $(f, \phi_1 \otimes \phi_2)$ is good (Definition 3.1.3), then 
    \[
        J^V(f , \phi_1 \otimes \phi_2)
        = \sum_\pi J^V_\pi(f, \phi_1 \otimes \phi_2),
    \]
    where the sum runs over all irreducible cupsidal automorphic 
    representations of $G^V(\mathbb A)$.
    The right hand side is absolutely convergent.

nodes.name: Proposition 5.2.5: General linear spectral decomposition
nodes.statement:
If the test function $(f', \phi')$ is good (Definition 3.2.4), then
\[
    I(f', \phi') = \sum_{\Pi} I_\Pi(f', \phi')
\]
where the sum runs over all irreducible cuspidal 
automorphic representations of $G'(\mathbb A)$ with
central character trivial on $A_{G'}^\infty$.
The right hand side is absolutely convergent.

nodes.name: Proposition 2.4.10: Orbit matching
nodes.statement:
There is a natural bijection 
\[
  [X_{\textnormal{rss}}] \simeq \coprod_{V} [Y_{\textnormal{rss}}^V]
\]
such that $[\gamma, x, y]$ and $[\zeta, z]^V$ match 
if and only if they have the same invariants.

nodes.name: Proposition 3.1.5: Unitary geometric decomposition
nodes.statement:
For a good test function $(f, \phi_1 \otimes \phi_2)$, we have 
\[
    J(f, \phi_1 \otimes \phi_2)= \sum_{[\zeta, z] \in [Y_{\textnormal{rss}}] 
    }
    \int_{H(\mathbb A)}\int_{H(\mathbb A)}
    f(h^{-1}_2 \zeta h_1)
    (\overline{\omega(h^{-1}_2h_1)\phi_1} \otimes \phi_2)^\ddagger(zh_2)\,dh_1\,dh_2,
\]
and both sides converge absolutely.

nodes.name: Proposition 3.2.9: General linear geometric decomposition
nodes.statement:
For good test functions $(f', \phi')$, we have
\[
    I(f', \phi') = \Delta_{H_1}^{*,-1} \Delta_{H_2}^{*,-1} \sum_{[\gamma, x, y] \in [X_{\textnormal{rss}}]}
    \prod_v \mathrm{Orb}([\xi, x, y], f_v', 
    \phi_v'),
\]
where $\xi$ is an element of $\mathrm{GL}_n(L)$ such
that $\gamma = \xi\sigma_{L/K}(\xi)^{-1}$, and
the product of local orbital integrals does
not depend on the choice of $\xi$.

nodes.name: Proposition 4.3.2: Existence of transfers
nodes.statement:
Suppose that $(f', \phi')$ and $(f, \phi_1 \otimes
\phi_2)$ are split smooth transfer of each
other as in Definition 4.3.1.
Assume that $S$ and $R^V$ are compatible as in
Definition 4.1.6. For $[\gamma, x, y] \in X_{\textnormal{rss}}$
and $[\zeta, z]^V \in Y_{\textnormal{rss}}^V$ which match
in the sense of Proposition 2.4.10, 
we have
\[
    \mathrm{Orb}([\xi, x, y], f', \phi')
    = \mathrm{Orb}([\zeta, z]^V, f, \phi_1 \otimes \phi_2)
\]
for any $\xi = (\xi_1, \xi_2) \in \mathrm{GL}_n(L)$ such
that $\gamma = (\gamma_1, \gamma_1^{-1}) = 
\xi\sigma_{L/K}(\xi)^{-1} = (\xi_1\xi_2^{-1},
\xi_2\xi_1^{-1})$.
